units.title: The Cyrillic alphabet: familiar shapes and false friends
goals: Read the fourteen letters 'а', 'в', 'е', 'и', 'і', 'к', 'м', 'н', 'о', 'р', 'с', 'т', 'у', 'х' in capital and small form, and say their names
Tell the false friends from the English letters they resemble: 'в', 'е', 'н', 'р', 'с', 'у', 'х', 'и'
Say the six vowel sounds of Ukrainian and tell 'и' from 'і'
Read the stress mark and know that it shows the stressed syllable and is not part of the spelling
Read aloud short words and sentences written only with these letters
grammar: Writing systems: an alphabet of 33 letters in which each letter stands for one sound or a small set of sounds
Letters that look and sound like English letters: 'а', 'к', 'м', 'о', 'т'
False friends, letters whose shape matches an English letter but whose sound does not: 'в', 'е', 'н', 'р', 'с', 'у', 'х', and 'и' and 'і'
The six vowel sounds 'а', 'о', 'у', 'е', 'и', 'і', all full and steady
The stress mark, the combining acute accent written after the stressed vowel of a word of two or more syllables
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each letter
letter names and spelling short names aloud
the first sentences without a verb ('Ма́ма тут.')

units.title: The Cyrillic alphabet: new shapes
goals: Read the letters 'б', 'г', 'ґ', 'д', 'ж', 'з', 'л', 'п', 'ф', 'ц', 'ч', 'ш', 'щ' and say their names
Tell 'г' from 'ґ' and read 'дж' and 'дз' as single sounds
Keep voiced consonants voiced at the end of a word, as in 'хліб'
Recognize the handwritten and italic forms that look different from printed letters
grammar: Letters with new shapes and their sounds: 'б', 'д', 'ж', 'з', 'л', 'п', 'ф', 'ц', 'ч', 'ш', 'щ'
'г' [ɦ], a voiced 'h', and 'ґ' [g], a hard 'g'
The two-letter sounds 'дж' and 'дз'
Voiced consonants stay voiced at the end of a word and before most consonants
The pointing word 'це' and the question 'Що це?'
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each new letter
everyday things and food named with the letters learned so far
spelling names aloud with the full set of consonants

units.title: Я, ю, є, ї, й, the soft sign and the apostrophe
goals: Read the letters 'й', 'я', 'ю', 'є', 'ї' and 'ь', completing the alphabet
Explain the two jobs of 'я', 'ю' and 'є': a 'y' sound plus a vowel, or a vowel that softens the consonant before it
Explain what the soft sign and the apostrophe do, as in 'день', 'ім’я́' and 'м’я́со'
Read doubled consonants such as the 'тт' of 'життя́' as long sounds
Read any Ukrainian word aloud from its spelling
grammar: 'й' [j] and the letters 'я', 'ю', 'є', 'ї', which add [j] at the start of a word, after a vowel and after the apostrophe
Hard and soft consonants; 'я', 'ю', 'є', 'і' and 'ь' soften the consonant before them, while 'е' and 'и' leave it hard
'ьо' and 'йо', the two ways of writing [jɔ] or a soft consonant plus 'о'
The apostrophe after 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м', 'ф' and 'р', which keeps the consonant hard and the [j] separate
Doubled consonant letters as long consonants ('життя́', 'знання́')
vocabulary_themes: words chosen only to illustrate each new letter and mark
a procedure for reading a word never seen before

units.title: Stress, the stress mark and the flow of speech
goals: Count the syllables of a word and find its stressed syllable from the stress mark
Explain why Ukrainian stress must be learned with each word and why it can move between forms ('рука́', 'ру́ки')
Tell apart words that differ only in stress ('за́мок', 'замо́к')
Choose between 'у' and 'в', 'і' and 'й', and 'з', 'із' and 'зі' to keep speech flowing
grammar: Syllables and the stressed syllable; unstressed vowels keep their full sound, unlike English
Free and mobile stress: no rule predicts it, it can fall on any syllable and it can move in other forms of the same word
Words told apart by stress alone
How this course writes stress: the mark on every word of two or more syllables, none on words of one syllable, ignored when you type an answer
Euphony: the alternations 'у'/'в', 'і'/'й' and 'з'/'із'/'зі', chosen by the sounds around them
vocabulary_themes: words that show stress on the first, middle and last syllable
pairs of words that differ only in stress
short words whose form depends on the sounds around them

units.title: How Ukrainian works: nouns, gender and cases
goals: Name the parts of speech and the terms of grammar used in this course, in English and in Ukrainian
Explain that Ukrainian has no articles and usually no word for 'is' in the present
Tell the gender of most nouns from their ending, and make adjectives agree with them
Explain what a case is, name the seven cases and say what each one does
Recognize the sound alternations inside words ('кіт', 'кота́'; 'кни́га', 'у кни́зі')
grammar: Parts of speech and the vocabulary of grammar ('іме́нник', 'прикме́тник', 'відмі́нок', 'рід', 'одни́на', 'множина́')
No articles; no present-tense word for 'is' and the rare use of 'є'; word order that is free but carries emphasis
Gender (masculine, feminine, neuter) from the ending, with natural gender winning; singular and plural
The seven cases: nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, instrumental, locative and vocative, with their questions and jobs
Alternations: 'о' and 'е' becoming 'і' in a closed syllable, and 'г', 'к', 'х' becoming 'з', 'ц', 'с' before '-і'
Questions with intonation and 'чи', and negation with 'не'
vocabulary_themes: the technical words for grammar, in English and Ukrainian
the small function words used in every sentence ('не', 'чи', 'але́', 'де')

units.title: How Ukrainian works: verbs, aspect and address
goals: Explain how a verb is built from a stem and an ending that shows the person and number of the subject
Recognize the two present-tense conjugations from the model verbs 'чита́ти' and 'говори́ти'
Explain aspect, the difference between imperfective and perfective verbs, and the map of tenses the course will teach
Use the subject pronouns and choose between 'ти' and 'ви'
grammar: The infinitive in '-ти', the stem, the personal endings, and the two conjugations
One present tense, a past tense that agrees in gender, and three ways to express the future
Aspect: every verb is imperfective or perfective, and most come in pairs ('чита́ти', 'прочита́ти')
Moods: indicative, imperative and conditional; reflexive verbs in '-ся'
Subject pronouns ('я', 'ти', 'він', 'вона́', 'воно́', 'ми', 'ви', 'вони́'), when they are dropped, and the address system: 'ти', 'ви', 'пан', 'па́ні'
vocabulary_themes: the technical words for verbs, in English and Ukrainian
the subject pronouns and the forms of address

units.title: Greetings, introductions and the vocative
goals: Greet people at different times of day and say goodbye
Introduce yourself, ask someone's name and say that you are pleased to meet them
Say where you are from and what nationality you are
Address people correctly with the vocative and with 'па́не' and 'па́ні'
Use basic politeness expressions and say what each one literally means
grammar: The vocative of first names: '-а' becomes '-о', a hard consonant takes '-е', '-й' becomes '-ю', '-я' becomes '-ю' or '-є'
Formal address: 'па́не' and 'па́ні' with the vocative of a first name, and a first name with a patronymic
Sentences without 'is': 'Я кана́дець.', 'Вона́ украї́нка.'
Fixed formulas met whole: 'Мене́ зва́ти...', 'Як тебе́ зва́ти?', 'Я з Кана́ди.', 'Як спра́ви?'
vocabulary_themes: nationalities, with a form for a man and a form for a woman

units.title: People and things: 'це', adjectives and possessives
goals: Point at and name people and things with 'це' and ask 'Хто це?' and 'Що це?'
Describe people and things with adjectives that agree in gender and number
Say whose something is with 'мій', 'твій', 'наш', 'ваш', 'його́', 'її́' and 'ї́хній'
Name professions in the form for a man and the form for a woman
grammar: 'Це' as a pointer, invariable, and the questions 'Хто це?', 'Що це?', 'Яки́й?'
Adjective agreement in the nominative: hard stems ('нови́й', 'нова́', 'нове́', 'нові́') and soft stems ('си́ній', 'си́ня', 'си́нє', 'си́ні')
The nominative plural of nouns: '-и', '-і', '-а'
Possessive pronouns, and 'його́', 'її́', 'їх' as invariable genitive forms of the personal pronouns
Feminine forms of professions ('лі́кар', 'лі́карка'; 'вчи́тель', 'вчи́телька')
vocabulary_themes: basic adjectives of size, age and quality

units.title: The present tense: work, study and languages
goals: Conjugate regular verbs of both conjugations in the present
Say what you do, where you work and which languages you speak
Ask and answer questions with 'як', 'чому́' and 'тому́ що'
Describe how you do something with adverbs
grammar: The first conjugation, including '-ува-' verbs ('працюва́ти', 'працю́ю') and stem changes ('писа́ти', 'пишу́'; 'жи́ти', 'живу́')
The second conjugation, including the 'л' added after 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м', 'ф' ('роби́ти', 'роблю́'; 'люби́ти', 'люблю́')
Which conjugation a verb follows, and the stress of its present forms
Adverbs of manner and degree; 'говори́ти украї́нською', met as a fixed phrase
vocabulary_themes: everyday verbs of work, study and thought

units.title: Food, drink and the accusative
goals: Order food and drink in a café or restaurant
Say what you want, eat, drink and see
Form the accusative of nouns and adjectives in the singular
Ask for the bill and wish someone a good meal
grammar: The accusative singular: '-у'/'-ю' for feminine nouns in '-а'/'-я'; masculine inanimate and neuter unchanged; masculine animate in '-а'/'-я'
Adjectives in the accusative ('смачну́ ка́ву', 'смачни́й суп')
Irregular presents: 'хоті́ти' ('хо́чу', 'хо́чеш'), 'ї́сти' ('їм', 'їси́', 'їдя́ть'), 'пи́ти' ('п’ю', 'п’єш')
Service phrases: 'Мо́жна...?', 'Мені́..., будь ла́ска', 'ка́ва з молоко́м', 'Смачно́го!'

units.title: Numbers, age and prices
goals: Count from 0 to 100 and give a phone number
Say how old you are
Ask for and understand prices in hryvnias
Use the right form of a noun after a number
grammar: Cardinal numbers 0 to 100: the teens in '-на́дцять', the tens, 'со́рок' and 'дев’яно́сто'
'Оди́н', 'одна́', 'одне́' and 'два', 'дві' agree in gender
The noun after a number: 1 takes the nominative singular, 2 to 4 the nominative plural, 5 and above a form met whole for now ('рік', 'ро́ки', 'ро́ків'; 'гри́вня', 'гри́вні', 'гри́вень')
Age with 'Мені́... ро́ків' and prices with 'Скі́льки ко́штує?', met as fixed patterns

units.title: Where things are: the locative, the city and the home
goals: Name places in a city and rooms in a home
Say where someone or something is with 'у', 'в' and 'на'
Form the locative of nouns and adjectives in the singular
Choose between 'у' and 'на' for places
grammar: The locative singular after 'у'/'в' and 'на', answering 'де?'
Endings: '-і' for most nouns, '-у'/'-ю' for many masculine nouns with stems in 'к', 'г', 'х' ('у па́рку')
Alternations before '-і': 'апте́ка', 'в апте́ці'; 'стіл', 'на столі́'
Adjectives in the locative ('у вели́кому мі́сті', 'у ва́нній')
'у' versus 'на' with places ('в Украї́ні', 'на робо́ті', 'на по́шті')

units.title: Going places: direction and the accusative
goals: Say where you are going with 'у', 'в' or 'на' and the accusative
Choose between 'іти́' and 'ї́хати'
Ask for and give simple directions
Tell 'де?' from 'куди́?'
grammar: Direction: 'у'/'в'/'на' with the accusative ('у парк', 'на вокза́л') against location with the locative
The present of 'іти́' ('іду́', 'іде́ш') and 'ї́хати' ('ї́ду', 'ї́деш'): on foot and by vehicle, in one direction now
'Могти́' ('мо́жу', 'мо́жеш') with an infinitive
Directions given in the present tense ('Ви йдете́ пря́мо, по́тім поверта́єте ліво́руч')

units.title: Family, possession and the genitive
goals: Talk about your family
Say what you have and do not have with 'у ме́не є' and 'у ме́не нема́є'
Say whose something is with the genitive and with 'чий'
Address family members in the vocative
grammar: The genitive singular: '-и'/'-і' for feminine nouns; '-а'/'-я' or '-у'/'-ю' for masculine nouns and how to choose; '-а'/'-я' for neuter nouns
Adjectives and possessives in the genitive ('мого́ бра́та', 'моє́ї сестри́')
Possession and absence: 'У ме́не є...', 'У ме́не нема́є...' with the genitive; the forms 'у ньо́го', 'у не́ї', 'у них'
The genitive after 'без', 'для', 'бі́ля', 'з' (from) and 'до'; 'чий', 'чия́', 'чиє́', 'чиї́'
The vocative of family words ('ма́мо', 'та́ту', 'си́ну', 'бабу́сю')

units.title: Daily routine, telling the time and reflexive verbs
goals: Describe a typical day
Tell the time and say at what time something happens
Use reflexive verbs in '-ся'
Say how often you do something, including 'ніко́ли не'
grammar: Reflexive verbs: the suffix '-ся' or '-сь', its meaning, and the pronunciation of '-ться' and '-шся'
Telling the time with feminine ordinal numerals: 'Котра́ годи́на?', 'Пе́рша.', 'О котрі́й?', 'О сьо́мій.', 'пів на во́сьму'
Parts of the day as adverbs ('вра́нці', 'уве́чері', 'вночі́')
Frequency adverbs and the double negative 'ніко́ли не'

units.title: Shopping, clothes and colors
goals: Ask for clothes in a size and a color
Point things out with 'цей' and 'той'
Ask what something costs and say whether it is cheap or expensive
Ask permission with 'мо́жна' and an infinitive
grammar: Demonstratives 'цей', 'ця', 'це', 'ці' and 'той', 'та', 'те', 'ті' in the nominative and accusative
Color adjectives and their agreement, including plural-only nouns ('штани́', 'гро́ші')
Predicative words with an infinitive: 'мо́жна приміря́ти?'
Prices with the plural verb ('Скі́льки ко́штують?')

units.title: Weather, seasons and plans: the future with 'бу́ду'
goals: Talk about the weather and the seasons
Name the days of the week and say on which day something happens
Talk about plans with the future 'бу́ду' plus an infinitive
Invite someone and accept or decline
grammar: The compound future of imperfective verbs: 'бу́ду', 'бу́деш', 'бу́де', 'бу́демо', 'бу́дете', 'бу́дуть' with an infinitive
Days of the week with 'у' and the accusative ('у субо́ту')
Weather: predicative words ('те́пло', 'хо́лодно') and 'Іде́ дощ.', 'Іде́ сніг.'
Seasons as adverbs ('взи́мку', 'навесні́', 'влі́тку', 'восени́')
vocabulary_themes: days of the week and seasons

units.title: A1 consolidation
goals: Combine the skills of A1 in realistic conversations
Introduce yourself and your family in detail
Handle simple situations: a café, a shop, directions, small talk
Review the cases met so far and how to choose between them
grammar: Review: nominative, vocative, accusative, locative and genitive singular, and when each is used
Review: the present of both conjugations, reflexive verbs and the future with 'бу́ду'
Connecting sentences with 'і', 'а', 'але́', 'або́', 'бо' and 'тому́'
Two ways to say 'to have': 'у ме́не є' and 'ма́ти'
Common beginner errors: 'и' and 'і', location against direction, gender agreement

units.title: The past tense
goals: Say what you did yesterday and last weekend
Form the past tense of any verb, agreeing with the gender of the subject
Ask and answer questions about past events
Use past time markers
grammar: The past: stem plus '-в', '-ла', '-ло', '-ли', agreeing in gender and number, not person
Past forms of 'бу́ти', 'іти́', 'могти́', 'ї́сти' and of stems ending in a consonant ('ніс', 'несла́')
'Не було́' with the genitive, the past of 'нема́є'
Time markers: 'вчо́ра', 'позавчо́ра', 'мину́лого ти́жня', 'рік тому́'

units.title: Aspect: imperfective and perfective
goals: Explain what aspect expresses and choose between imperfective and perfective verbs in the past
Recognize how aspect pairs are formed
Know that a perfective verb has no present and that its present-looking forms mean the future
Talk about tasks begun, finished and not yet done
grammar: Aspect: process, repetition and general fact against a single completed result
Forming pairs: a prefix ('писа́ти', 'написа́ти'), a change of suffix ('дава́ти', 'да́ти'; 'купува́ти', 'купи́ти'), different stems ('бра́ти', 'взя́ти')
Aspect in the past ('Я чита́в.' against 'Я прочита́в.') and words that point to one or the other
'Почина́ти' and 'закі́нчувати' with an imperfective infinitive

units.title: The future: imperfective and perfective
goals: Talk about plans, intentions and promises
Form the two imperfective futures and the perfective future
Use the future after 'коли́' and 'якщо́'
Plan a trip
grammar: The compound future ('бу́ду чита́ти') and the synthetic future ('чита́тиму', 'чита́тимеш')
The perfective future ('прочита́ю') formed like a present
The future in clauses with 'коли́' and 'якщо́', where English uses the present
Time phrases: 'че́рез ти́ждень', 'пі́сля робо́ти', 'насту́пного ро́ку'

units.title: The dative: likes, gifts, birthdays and dates
goals: Say what you like with 'подо́батися'
Say to whom you give, say or send something
Say what you need or may do with 'тре́ба' and 'мо́жна'
Name the months and give dates
grammar: The dative singular: '-і' for feminine nouns, '-ові'/'-еві'/'-єві' or '-у'/'-ю' for masculine nouns, '-у'/'-ю' for neuter nouns; adjectives in '-ому' and '-ій'
Dative pronouns ('мені́', 'тобі́', 'йому́', 'їй', 'нам', 'вам', 'їм')
The person as dative: 'Мені́ подо́бається...', 'Мені́ тре́ба...', 'Мені́ хо́лодно', and age explained
Dates: 'Яке́ сього́дні число́?', 'пе́рше тра́вня', 'пе́ршого тра́вня', with ordinal numerals

units.title: The instrumental: work, hobbies and company
goals: Say what you work as and what you want to become
Talk about hobbies and sport with 'займа́тися', 'цікави́тися' and 'гра́ти'
Say with whom and by what means you do something
Describe position with 'над', 'під', 'між', 'пе́ред' and 'за'
grammar: The instrumental singular: '-ою'/'-ею'/'-єю' for feminine nouns, '-ом'/'-ем'/'-єм' for masculine and neuter nouns, '-ю' with a doubled consonant for feminine nouns in a consonant
Adjectives and pronouns in the instrumental ('з нови́м дру́гом', 'зі мно́ю', 'з не́ю')
Uses: company with 'з', means ('авто́бусом'), role after 'працюва́ти', 'бу́ти', 'ста́ти', and verbs that take it
'Украї́нською' explained as the instrumental of 'украї́нська мо́ва'

units.title: Pronouns in every case, 'свій', and 'someone' and 'no one'
goals: Use every personal pronoun in every case, including the forms with 'н' after a preposition
Choose between 'свій' and 'його́', 'її́', 'їх'
Talk about someone, something and somewhere with '-сь' and 'будь-'
Use negative pronouns with the double negative ('Я нікого́ не ба́чу')
grammar: The full declension of 'я', 'ти', 'він', 'вона́', 'воно́', 'ми', 'ви', 'вони́' and of 'себе́'
'Свій' for something that belongs to the subject
Indefinite pronouns and adverbs: 'хтось', 'щось', 'десь', 'коли́сь', 'яки́йсь', 'будь-хто'
Negative pronouns and adverbs with 'не': 'ніхто́', 'нічо́го', 'ніде́', 'нія́кий', and 'ні з ким'
'Весь', 'сам', 'ко́жен', 'і́нший'

units.title: The imperative: instructions and recipes
goals: Give instructions, advice and invitations
Form the imperative for 'ти', 'ви' and 'ми'
Choose the aspect of an imperative
Follow and give a recipe
grammar: Forming the imperative from the present stem: '-й' ('чита́й'), '-и' ('пиши́'), no ending ('ріж'); '-те' for 'ви', '-мо' for 'ми'
Irregular imperatives: 'їж', 'пий', 'дай', 'будь'
Aspect in the imperative: perfective for one specific act, imperfective for invitations, general advice and negative commands
'Дава́й' and 'дава́йте' with an infinitive or a future, and 'неха́й' or 'хай' for the third person

units.title: The plural in every case: markets and quantities
goals: Use nouns and adjectives in the plural in every case
Form the genitive plural, including the forms with no ending
Use numbers and quantity words with the right noun forms
Shop at a market
grammar: Plural endings: genitive '-ів', '-ей' or no ending with an inserted vowel ('пля́шок', 'сесте́р'); dative '-ам'/'-ям'; instrumental '-ами'/'-ями'; locative '-ах'/'-ях'
The plural accusative: nominative for things, genitive for people and animals
Adjectives in the plural ('-і', '-их', '-им', '-ими')
Numbers with nouns in full; 'бага́то', 'ма́ло', 'кі́лька', 'до́сить' with the genitive
'Люди́на', 'лю́ди' and 'дити́на', 'ді́ти'
vocabulary_themes: fruit and vegetables at the market

units.title: Health and the body
goals: Name the parts of the body
Say what hurts and how you feel
Talk to a doctor and a pharmacist
Give and understand advice with 'тре́ба', 'му́сити' and 'пови́нен'
grammar: 'У ме́не боли́ть...' and 'У ме́не боля́ть...': the possessor in the genitive and the body part as subject
The irregular plural 'о́чі' against the regular 'ву́ха'
Obligation and advice: 'му́сити', 'пови́нен', 'тре́ба', 'ва́рто', with the imperative
'Як ти почува́єшся?' and 'Що з тобо́ю?'

units.title: Travel and the verbs of motion
goals: Choose between a verb of motion in one direction and its partner for movement in general
Say where you go regularly and where you went and came back from
Travel by train, plane and taxi
Use 'піти́' and 'пої́хати' for setting off
grammar: Pairs of motion verbs: 'іти́', 'ходи́ти'; 'ї́хати', 'ї́здити'; 'леті́ти', 'літа́ти'; 'нести́', 'носи́ти'; 'везти́', 'вози́ти'; 'бі́гти', 'бі́гати'
One direction now or on the way, against habit, round trips, ability and movement in general
'Ходи́в' and 'ї́здив' for a completed round trip; 'піти́' and 'пої́хати' for setting off
Consonant changes in the first person: 'ходжу́', 'ї́жджу', 'ношу́', 'вожу́'

units.title: Comparing: comparatives and superlatives
goals: Compare people, places and things
Form comparatives in '-іший' and '-ший', including the irregular ones
Form superlatives with 'най-'
Compare actions with comparative adverbs
grammar: Comparatives: '-іший' ('нові́ший'), '-ший' with stem changes ('ви́щий', 'до́вший', 'ле́гший'), and 'кра́щий', 'гі́рший', 'бі́льший', 'ме́нший'
'Ніж' with the nominative and 'за' with the accusative ('ви́щий за ме́не')
Superlatives with 'най-' and 'якнай-'; 'більш' and 'менш' with an adjective
Comparative adverbs ('кра́ще', 'шви́дше'); 'таки́й..., як' and 'так са́мо, як'
vocabulary_themes: adjectives of size, age, difficulty and temperature

units.title: The conditional: polite requests, wishes and 'if'
goals: Make polite requests and offers with 'б' or 'би'
Talk about wishes and imagined situations
Tell real conditions with 'якщо́' from unreal ones with 'якби́'
Give advice with 'На тво́єму мі́сці я б...'
grammar: The conditional: the past form plus the particle 'би' or 'б', one form for present and past
Polite requests: 'Я б хоті́ла...', 'Чи не могли́ б ви...?'
Unreal conditions with 'якби́' against real conditions with 'якщо́' and the future
The spelling 'якби́' against 'як би'

units.title: A2 consolidation
goals: Combine the skills of A2 in realistic conversations
Tell what happened, what is happening and what will happen, choosing aspect
Handle situations: travel, health, shopping, invitations
Review the whole case system
grammar: Review: the seven cases in the singular and plural, with the noun declension tables
Review: past, aspect, the futures, the imperative and the conditional
Review: verbs of motion and the choice between location and direction
Conversation strategies: asking for explanations and repetitions
vocabulary_themes: asking for help with the language

units.title: Numerals in every case, years and statistics
goals: Say large numbers, years and centuries
Decline cardinal numerals and use them with nouns in every case
Use collective numerals, fractions and percentages
Read and discuss simple statistics
grammar: Declension of cardinal numerals ('двох', 'двом', 'двома́'; 'п’ятьо́х', 'п’ятьма́')
Years and centuries: only the last word is an ordinal ('у ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому ро́ці')
Collective numerals ('дво́є', 'тро́є') and 'о́бидва', 'о́бидві'
Fractions, 'полови́на', 'чверть', 'півтора́' and percentages

units.title: Telling a story: aspect in narration
goals: Tell a life story or an anecdote in the past
Use perfective verbs for a sequence of events and imperfective verbs for background
Use 'по́ки', 'як ті́льки' and 'коли́' to link events
Tell 'за годи́ну', 'протя́гом годи́ни' and 'че́рез годи́ну' apart
grammar: Aspect in narration: chains of perfectives, imperfective background, interruption
Time clauses with 'коли́', 'по́ки', 'як ті́льки'
Time expressions: 'за' with the accusative, 'протя́гом' with the genitive, 'че́рез' with the accusative
Life events: 'народи́тися', 'ви́рости', 'одружи́тися'

units.title: Prefixed verbs of motion
goals: Use motion verbs with prefixes for arriving, leaving, entering, crossing and passing
Form the aspect pairs of prefixed motion verbs
Use the prepositions that go with each prefix
Describe a route and a move to a new home
grammar: Prefixes 'при-', 'ви-', 'у-', 'за-', 'пере-', 'від-', 'до-', 'про-', 'під-', 'об-' with 'іти́' and 'ї́хати'
Aspect: a prefix on the one-direction verb makes a perfective ('прийти́'), on the general verb an imperfective ('прихо́дити')
Prefix and preposition pairs: 'ви́йти з', 'зайти́ до', 'перейти́ че́рез', 'дійти́ до', 'відійти́ від', 'пройти́ повз'
The spellings 'йти' and 'ї́хати' after a prefix ('прийти́', 'приї́хати')

units.title: Relative clauses and housing
goals: Describe people, places and things with relative clauses
Decline 'яки́й' in a relative clause
Use 'що', 'хто', 'де' and 'куди́' as relative words
Look for and rent an apartment
grammar: 'Яки́й', 'яка́', 'яке́', 'які́' as relative pronouns: gender and number from the noun, case from the clause
'Що' as an invariable relative word, and 'той, хто' and 'те, що'
Relative 'де', 'куди́', 'зві́дки' and 'чий'
Commas around relative clauses

units.title: Wishes, requests and purpose with 'щоб'
goals: Say what you want someone else to do
Pass on requests and demands
Express purpose with 'щоб' and 'для то́го, щоб'
Express hopes and fears
grammar: 'Щоб' with the past form for a wish or request about another subject ('Я хо́чу, щоб ти прийшо́в')
Same subject: the infinitive ('Я хо́чу прийти́')
Purpose: 'щоб' with an infinitive or with the past form
Verbs and predicative words that take 'щоб': 'проси́ти', 'вимага́ти', 'ва́жливо', 'необхі́дно'

units.title: Passive participles and impersonal sentences
goals: Understand and use passive participles
Use the impersonal forms in '-но' and '-то' ('Музе́й відчи́нено.')
Understand signs, notices and short news items
Use impersonal sentences ('Мені́ не спи́ться.')
grammar: Passive participles in '-ний', '-ений', '-тий', declined like adjectives
The impersonal forms in '-но' and '-то' with the object in the accusative
The passive in '-ся' for processes ('Буди́нок буду́ється.')
Impersonal sentences; relative clauses in place of the rare active participles in '-учий' and '-ючий'

units.title: Adverbial participles
goals: Form imperfective adverbial participles in '-учи' and '-ючи'
Form perfective adverbial participles in '-вши' and '-ши'
Use them for simultaneous and earlier actions by the same subject
Tell a travel story in a written style
grammar: Imperfective adverbial participles from the present stem: 'чита́ючи', 'пи́шучи', 'ідучи́', reflexive '-чись'
Perfective adverbial participles from the past stem: 'прочита́вши', 'прийшо́вши'
The same-subject rule and the comma
Written and spoken style: the adverbial participle against 'коли́'
vocabulary_themes: verbs of movement in the landscape

units.title: Work, institutions and formal letters
goals: Talk about jobs, applications and interviews
Write a formal letter or email
Address people formally in speech and in writing
Fill in forms and deal with institutions
grammar: Formal address: 'ви', 'Ви' in letters, 'Шано́вний па́не...' and 'Шано́вна па́ні...' with the vocative, surnames in '-енко'
The structure of a formal letter: greeting, request, closing 'З пова́гою'
Formal requests: 'Прошу́...', 'Про́симо...'
Nouns of common gender ('ко́лега') and verbal nouns in '-ння'

units.title: Opinions and argument
goals: Give and ask for opinions
Agree and disagree politely
Structure an argument with linking words
Express cause, concession and consequence
grammar: Opinion verbs with 'що': 'вважа́ти', 'ду́мати', 'зда́ватися'
Cause: 'бо', 'тому́ що', 'оскі́льки', 'че́рез' and 'завдяки́'
Concession and contrast: 'хоча́', 'незважа́ючи на', 'проте́', 'одна́к'
Consequence and structure: 'тому́', 'о́тже', 'по-пе́рше', 'з одно́го бо́ку'

units.title: Reported speech
goals: Report statements, questions and requests
Keep the tense of the original statement, as Ukrainian does
Use 'чи' for reported yes or no questions and 'щоб' for reported requests
Signal doubt about reported words with 'ні́бито' and 'мо́вляв'
grammar: Reported statements with 'що' and no change of tense
Reported questions with 'чи' and question words
Reported requests and commands with 'щоб' and the past form
Verbs of saying, and the particles 'ні́бито' and 'мо́вляв'; direct speech in quotation marks

units.title: Verbal prefixes and the finer points of aspect
goals: Recognize the meanings that prefixes add to verbs
Form secondary imperfectives
Choose aspect in negation, in questions about experience and in instructions
Express nuances such as beginning, doing for a while and doing to excess
grammar: Prefix meanings: 'за-' (start), 'по-' (a while), 'пере-' (again, too much), 'до-' (to the end), 'на-...-ся' and 'ви-...-ся' (to one's fill), 'роз-...-ся' (to burst into)
Secondary imperfectives ('переписа́ти', 'перепи́сувати')
Aspect in negation, in general questions and with a cancelled result
Verbs of managing, trying and getting used to

units.title: Word formation: diminutives, feminine forms and possessive adjectives
goals: Form and understand diminutive and affectionate forms
Form the feminine names of professions
Use possessive adjectives such as 'ма́мин' and 'та́тів'
Recognize families of words built on one root
grammar: Diminutive suffixes for nouns and adjectives, with their consonant changes ('рука́', 'руче́нька')
Feminine forms in '-ка', '-иця', '-иня'
Possessive adjectives in '-ин' and '-ів', with the vowel alternation
Roots, prefixes and suffixes in families of words

units.title: Idioms, proverbs and spoken Ukrainian
goals: Understand and use common idioms and proverbs
Use particles that add attitude: 'ж', 'же', 'хіба́', 'невже́', 'адже́', 'таки́'
Recognize features of everyday speech
Choose the register that suits a situation
grammar: Idioms and their literal meanings
Proverbs and their structures
Particles of emphasis, surprise and doubt
Interjections and the patterns of spoken Ukrainian

units.title: Ukrainian literature and poetry
goals: Read short passages of Ukrainian poetry and prose
Recognize poetic word order and poetic forms
Talk about writers and their works
Discuss the themes of classic Ukrainian literature
grammar: Poetic word order and the vocative in poetry
Poetic and older forms met in classic texts, for recognition
The vocabulary of literature: verse, line, rhyme, image

units.title: Formal writing and the language of the media
goals: Read news articles and official texts
Write a formal summary or report
Use the prepositional phrases of official style
Use the standard forms that formal Ukrainian requires
grammar: Nominal style and verbal nouns
Prepositional phrases of official style: 'відпові́дно до', 'згі́дно з', 'у зв’язку́ з', 'з мето́ю', 'що́до'
The impersonal forms in '-но' and '-то' in official writing
Parenthetical words and their commas

units.title: History, culture and identity
goals: Read and discuss texts about Ukrainian history
Talk about traditions and holidays
Discuss language and identity
Use the historical present in narration
grammar: The historical present in narration
Centuries and dates in historical writing
Review of the noun declensions as a system, with the four declension classes of Ukrainian grammar

units.title: Capstone
goals: Combine the skills of the whole course in extended conversations and texts
Present and defend a view in speech and writing
Adjust register from friendly to formal
Review your progress and plan further learning
grammar: Review: cases, aspect and verbs of motion
Review: complex sentences with 'щоб', 'якби́', relative clauses and adverbial participles
Review: register, address and the vocative
